title: Reverse a Linked List Section
description:
Reverse the nodes of a singly linked list from position l to position r (1-based, inclusive) and print the whole list afterwards. Nodes outside that range stay where they are.

Input format
Line 1: n, l and r separated by spaces.
Line 2: the n node values in order.

Output format
The resulting list on one line, values separated by single spaces.
hints: Walk to the node just before position l. That node must end up pointing at the old r-th node.
Reverse the r-l+1 nodes one at a time by repeatedly moving the node after the section start to the front of the section.
Keep four things: the node before the section, the first node of the section (which becomes its last), and while reversing a prev/current pair. A dummy head avoids special-casing l = 1.
